qualifiers: a named cheese, not a dish

answers.name: Cheddar
answers.fact: Named after the Somerset village of Cheddar, where it was aged in caves.

answers.name: Mozzarella
answers.fact: Traditionally made from water buffalo milk in southern Italy.

answers.name: Parmesan
answers.fact: A wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano weighs around 40 kg.

answers.name: Brie
answers.fact: Brie de Meaux is said to have been crowned 'king of cheeses' at the 1815 Congress of Vienna.

answers.name: Feta
answers.fact: Protected in the EU since 2002: real feta comes from Greece.

answers.name: Gouda
answers.fact: Named after the Dutch city of Gouda, where it was traded.

answers.name: Swiss cheese
answers.fact: In the US, 'Swiss cheese' means an Emmental-style cheese with holes.

answers.name: Cream cheese
answers.fact: 'Philadelphia' cream cheese was actually first made in New York.

answers.name: Blue cheese
answers.fact: The blue veins are a mould, Penicillium roqueforti.

answers.name: Halloumi
answers.fact: Squeaks against your teeth, and doesn't melt when grilled.

answers.name: Roquefort
answers.fact: By law it must be aged in the Combalou caves of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon.

answers.name: Stinking Bishop
answers.fact: Washed in perry made from the Stinking Bishop pear.

answers.name: Camembert
answers.fact: Its round wooden box was invented in the 1890s so it could travel.

answers.name: Gorgonzola
answers.fact: Named after a town near Milan.

answers.name: Stilton
answers.fact: Can only be made in three English counties, and not in the village of Stilton.

answers.name: Ricotta
answers.fact: 'Recooked' in Italian: it's made from leftover whey.

answers.name: Mascarpone
answers.fact: The creamy base of tiramisu.

answers.name: Provolone
answers.fact: Often aged hanging from ropes.

answers.name: Pecorino
answers.fact: Pecorino Romano was a ration for Roman soldiers.

answers.name: Emmental
answers.fact: The holes, called 'eyes', come from gas made by bacteria.

answers.name: Gruyère
answers.fact: A key cheese in classic Swiss fondue.

answers.name: Manchego
answers.fact: Made only from the milk of Manchega sheep in La Mancha.

answers.name: Edam
answers.fact: Exported wrapped in red wax; legend says it was once fired as cannonballs.

answers.name: Havarti
answers.fact: First made by Danish farmer Hanne Nielsen in the 1800s.

answers.name: Monterey Jack
answers.fact: Named after Monterey, California, and businessman David Jacks.

answers.name: Colby
answers.fact: Named after the town of Colby, Wisconsin.

answers.name: Paneer
answers.fact: A fresh Indian cheese that holds its shape in curries.

answers.name: Cottage cheese
answers.fact: Its curds are rinsed to keep them mild.

answers.name: Burrata
answers.fact: Mozzarella on the outside, cream and shredded curd inside.

answers.name: Bocconcini
answers.fact: Bite-sized mozzarella balls; the name means 'little mouthfuls'.

answers.name: Wensleydale
answers.fact: Wallace and Gromit's favourite.

answers.name: Red Leicester
answers.fact: Coloured orange with annatto.

answers.name: Double Gloucester
answers.fact: Wheels of it are chased down Cooper's Hill in Gloucestershire's cheese-rolling race.

answers.name: Pepper Jack
answers.fact: Monterey Jack studded with chilli.

answers.name: American cheese
answers.fact: Processed cheese, patented by James L. Kraft in 1916.

answers.name: Queso fresco
answers.fact: 'Fresh cheese' in Spanish.

answers.name: Babybel
answers.fact: Mini Babybel launched in 1977 in its red wax coat.

answers.name: Taleggio
answers.fact: Has a pinkish washed rind and a fruity tang.

answers.name: Comté
answers.fact: France's most-produced protected cheese.

answers.name: Fontina
answers.fact: The star of Italian fondue, 'fonduta'.

answers.name: Asiago
answers.fact: Named after a plateau in the Veneto.

answers.name: Port Salut
answers.fact: First made by Trappist monks.

answers.name: Reblochon
answers.fact: The name comes from 're-milking': farmers secretly milked again to dodge taxes.

answers.name: Munster
answers.fact: The Alsace original is pungent; American 'Muenster' is mild.

answers.name: Limburger
answers.fact: Its smell comes from bacteria related to those behind foot odour.

answers.name: Jarlsberg
answers.fact: Norwegian, with big Emmental-style holes.

answers.name: Cotija
answers.fact: A crumbly Mexican cheese named after the town of Cotija.

answers.name: Labneh
answers.fact: Strained yoghurt cheese from the Middle East.

answers.name: Boursin
answers.fact: A garlic-and-herb cheese invented in Normandy in 1957.

answers.name: Danish blue
answers.fact: Invented in the early 1900s to rival Roquefort.

answers.name: Caerphilly
answers.fact: A crumbly Welsh cheese once popular with coal miners.

answers.name: Cheshire
answers.fact: Often called one of England's oldest named cheeses.

answers.name: Pont-l'Évêque
answers.fact: One of the oldest Normandy cheeses still made.

answers.name: Brunost
answers.fact: Norway's caramel-brown 'cheese', made by boiling down whey.

answers.name: Mimolette
answers.fact: A bright orange French ball whose rind is worked by tiny cheese mites.

answers.name: Tête de Moine
answers.fact: Shaved into frilly rosettes with a tool called a girolle.

answers.name: Casu marzu
answers.fact: A Sardinian cheese deliberately full of live insect larvae.

answers.name: Vieux-Boulogne
answers.fact: Named the smelliest cheese in the world in a 2004 UK study.

answers.name: Pule
answers.fact: Made from Balkan donkey milk, and among the priciest cheeses on Earth.

answers.name: Époisses
answers.fact: Washed in brandy; rumoured to be banned on Paris public transport (it isn't).

answers.name: Bitto
answers.fact: Some wheels of this Alpine cheese are aged for over a decade.

answers.name: Raclette
answers.fact: Melted at the table and scraped onto potatoes: 'racler' means to scrape.
